sections.html:
The required notice turns on the kind of tenancy and the reason for ending it. Wis. Stat. 704.17 sets the baseline for missed rent: at least 5 days when the tenancy is month-to-month, week-to-week, or a lease of one year or less, and at least 30 days when the lease runs past a year.

SituationMinimum notice
Unpaid rent, month-to-month or week-to-weekPay or vacate at least 5 days out. A month-to-month tenant in default can instead get a vacate notice at least 14 days out.
Unpaid rent, lease of one year or less, or year-to-yearPay or vacate at least 5 days out. A second default within one year allows a 14-day vacate notice.
Other breach or waste, month-to-monthRemedy or vacate at least 5 days out, or a 14-day vacate notice
Other breach or waste, lease of one year or lessRemedy or vacate at least 5 days out. A repeat within one year allows a 14-day vacate notice.
Any default, lease longer than one yearAt least 30 days to pay, repair or comply
Criminal or drug-related activityVacate at least 5 days out, with no chance to remedy
No-fault end of a month-to-month tenancyAt least 28 days, ending at the close of a rental period

Rent, for this purpose, includes past due rent plus late fees owed on it, so one pay-or-vacate notice can demand both.

sections.h2: How a tenant cures a default
sections.html:
For a breach that is not about rent, the tenant is treated as complying by taking reasonable steps to fix the problem right after receiving the notice and sticking with the repair diligently. Another way to comply: where money damages would protect the landlord, the tenant makes a reasonable offer to pay them in good faith. Both tests appear in 704.17(1p)(b), (2)(b) and (3)(a).

Rent on a lease longer than a year is stricter. Everything owed must be paid by the date in the notice. If the tenant repeats a breach within a year of an earlier notice, the cure period disappears and the landlord may serve a 14-day vacate notice.

  • Criminal activity that threatens other tenants, neighbors or the landlord, and drug-related criminal activity on or near the premises, can end a tenancy on 5 days' notice with no cure period.
  • That notice has to describe the activity, give the date, name those involved, and explain the tenant's right to contest it in court.
  • A tenant who is the victim of the criminal activity is carved out under 704.17(3m)(c).
  • Under Wis. Stat. 704.16(3), a landlord can end the tenancy of someone whose acts put another tenant in the same building at imminent risk of serious physical harm, on at least 5 days' written notice, once one of the listed court filings or orders exists.

Put it in writing and deliver it by one of the methods in Wis. Stat. 704.21. After the termination date in a properly given notice, the tenant has no right to remain.

  • Hand it to the tenant, or leave it at the tenant's usual home with a family member at least 14 years old who is told what it says.
  • Leave a copy with a competent person in charge of the premises and mail a copy to the tenant's last-known address.
  • If those fail despite reasonable diligence, post it in a conspicuous place on the premises and mail a copy.
  • Send it by registered or certified mail to the tenant's last-known address.
  • Serve it the way a summons is served under Wis. Stat. 801.11.

A notice that skips the listed methods can still count if the tenant actually got it, but whoever claims receipt must prove it by clear and convincing evidence. Certified mail has a court perk: under Wis. Stat. 799.40(1g), the post office's proof of mailing is enough to show proper notice when the landlord files. For 28-day notices, 704.19(7) counts the day of giving as day one, and mail within Wisconsin is treated as given on the second day after mailing.

sections.h2: Can a lease or a mistake change the rules?
sections.html:
A lease cannot cut these protections down, except on leases longer than one year. Under 704.17(5), lease terms on ending a tenancy that conflict with the section are void apart from that one exception. A lease term that runs against the criminal activity rule in subsection (3m) is void on every lease.

Small errors do not always sink a notice. A rent notice with the wrong amount stays valid unless the landlord's figure was intentionally wrong or the tenant paid or tendered what the tenant believes is due (704.17(4m)). For a notice ending a periodic tenancy, an error that does not mislead does not void it, and a wrong termination date makes the notice effective on the first proper date after the one stated (704.19(4), (5)).

The landlord still has to go to court. A proper notice ends the tenant's right to occupy, but removal happens through an eviction action, handled in Wisconsin as a small claims case under chapter 799. Wis. Stat. 799.40(1) lets the person entitled to possession, or an agent authorized in writing, start it.

Taking back past due rent after the notice or after filing does not force a dismissal (799.40(1m)). In an eviction, the summons return date lands 5 to 25 days after issue, and the tenant must be served at least 5 days before that date (799.05(3)(b)). If the landlord wins, the court orders a writ of restitution and the sheriff carries it out under Wis. Stat. 799.44(2) and 799.45.

sections.h2: How a tenant affects selling a rented house
sections.html:
A tenant not in default keeps exclusive possession until the lease ends or a periodic tenancy is terminated. Wis. Stat. 704.05(2) lets the landlord show the premises to prospective purchasers on advance notice and at reasonable times, unless both sides signed a lease provision saying otherwise.

An owner who wants the house empty at closing should match the notice to the tenancy before picking a closing date. A no-fault month-to-month notice needs 28 days and must end at the close of a rental period. A default on a lease longer than a year needs 30 days. Selling with the tenant in place skips the notice and court steps altogether, and that can be weighed against how long removal would take.

A practical order of work: confirm the tenancy type from the lease, write and serve the right notice, keep proof of delivery, and only then set a closing date you can realistically meet. A cash buyer who accepts the house occupied removes most of that timeline risk.

faqs.q: How many days is a Wisconsin eviction notice for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Five days for a month-to-month, week-to-week, or one-year-or-shorter tenancy, and 30 days for a lease longer than one year. A month-to-month tenant in default can alternatively receive a 14-day vacate notice. The notice must be in writing and delivered by a method in Wis. Stat. 704.21.

faqs.q: Can a Wisconsin landlord evict without giving a chance to fix the problem?
faqs.a: In some cases, yes. A tenant who repeats a breach within one year can get a 14-day vacate notice. Criminal activity that threatens health or safety, and drug-related criminal activity on or near the premises, allow a 5-day notice with no cure period. A tenant who is the victim of the activity is excluded.

faqs.q: How long is the notice to end a month-to-month tenancy with no fault?
faqs.a: At least 28 days, in writing, ending at the close of a rental period. If rent is payable more often than monthly, a notice equal to the rent-paying period is enough. The notice must say the landlord intends to end the tenancy and give the date.

faqs.q: Does a Wisconsin landlord have to mail the eviction notice?
faqs.a: No. Wis. Stat. 704.21 lists several methods: handing it to the tenant, leaving it with a family member or person in charge plus mailing, posting plus mailing, certified mail, or service like a summons. Certified mail helps in court because proof of mailing is enough to show notice.

faqs.q: Is a notice enough to remove a tenant in Wisconsin?
faqs.a: No. Once the notice period runs out, the landlord must file an eviction action in court. If the landlord wins, the court orders a writ of restitution and the sheriff removes the tenant. The sheriff must carry out the writ within 10 days of receiving it.
